correctness.rationale: The absorbing-diffusion scale and tail identities give \(q(x)=A\alpha x^{\alpha-1}\) and \(H(x)=x^{2-\alpha}/[A\alpha(2-\alpha)]\), proving the prescribed mean. The killed-diffusion Green/Kac second-moment recursion and integration by parts give \(V\prime(x)=2q(x)e^{H(x)}\int_x^\infty q(z)e^{-H(z)}\,dz\) (where \(V\prime\) denotes the derivative of variance), without an arbitrary boundary solution. Two substitutions produce the incomplete-Gamma integral; its integrand behaves as \(u^{2p-2}\), so \(p=1/2\), equivalently \(\alpha=2/3\), is the exact integrability threshold. Integration yields the sharp constants and subcritical remainder, while positive Fubini and a Beta integral evaluate the plateau. Spatial hitting-time convolution yields a bounded \(L^2\) centered martingale below the threshold. The standalone checker passed 198 symbolic/numerical assertions; finite tests are not proofs of the infinite limits.

value.rationale: In a prescribed-mean landscape with \(\mathbb E[T_x]=A x^\alpha\to\infty\), absolute timing variance nevertheless remains bounded at arbitrarily large initial distance exactly for \(0<\alpha<2/3\). The logarithmic marginal case, sharp polynomial coefficient, nonzero finite plateau and nondegenerate centered spatial limit delimit a meaningful timing-reliability design boundary beyond specifying mean arrival times. This is an evaluated natural invariant and complete three-regime classification, not a bare substitution or numeric table.
